rows.normative_requirement:
Every applicable formal release requiring signing or attestation must
produce an immutable machine-readable verification record containing,
at minimum:

- release identifier
- source revision
- artifact identifier and SHA-256 digest
- signature or attestation identifier
- signing mechanism
- signer or workload identity
- verification authority or workflow identity
- verification result
- verification timestamp
- applicable trust-policy or authorization reference

The verification record must establish both:

1. cryptographic validity of the signature or attestation; and
2. authorization of the signer or workload identity under RI-036-03.

A cryptographically valid signature from an unauthorized identity does
not satisfy EMS-CTRL-036.

The verification record must be bound to the authoritative release
manifest and retained with the authoritative release evidence.

The authoritative copy must reside in an approved immutable or
tamper-evident release-evidence store.

Acceptable immutability mechanisms include:

- immutable release artifacts;
- append-only or retention-protected evidence storage;
- cryptographically integrity-protected evidence records; or
- another EMS-approved mechanism providing equivalent tamper evidence.

Repository working-tree files alone are not authoritative immutable
verification evidence.

The verification record is subject to the Release Integrity evidence
retention requirements established by RI-037-02.

rows.normative_requirement: Release-integrity evidence for formal production releases must be retained for a minimum of seven years. This includes release manifests, checksum records, signing/attestation records, release approval records, and release verification records. Distributed release artifacts themselves must be retained for at least one year after release unless a longer period is required by contract, regulation, legal/audit hold, or controlled EMS policy. Material build outputs required to reproduce an active supported release must be retained for the supported life of that release or one year, whichever is longer. Legal, regulatory, contractual, or audit holds override normal deletion schedules.

rows.normative_requirement:
Formal releases must use Semantic Versioning 2.0.0.

The authoritative release version is expressed as:

MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH

with the optional lowercase "v" tag prefix governed by RI-038-03.

Prerelease identifiers and build metadata are governed by RI-038-04.

Migration and exception handling are governed by RI-038-05.

Historical tags are not rewritten solely to achieve compliance.

New formal releases that do not conform to the approved repository convention
and do not have an active approved exception are noncompliant with EMS-CTRL-038.

rows.normative_requirement:
The approved Semantic Versioning policy applies prospectively to all
new formal releases after the repository's EMS version-governance
effective date.

Existing historical tags are not required to be renamed, deleted, or
rewritten solely to comply with EMS-CTRL-038.

Each applicable repository must establish its approved release-tag
convention using one of the forms permitted by RI-038-03:

MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH

or

vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH

After that convention is established, new formal release tags must use
it consistently.

Historical nonconforming tags must be treated as legacy records and
must not be used as precedent for new releases.

A temporary exception to the approved versioning policy requires a
controlled exception record containing:

- repository
- requested deviation
- business or technical justification
- accountable owner
- approving EMS governance authority
- approval date
- effective date
- expiration or review date
- remediation or migration plan

Exceptions must be explicitly approved by the designated EMS governance
authority before the nonconforming formal release.

Exceptions must be time-bounded and reviewed no less than annually if
they remain active.

An expired, unapproved, or undocumented exception does not authorize a
nonconforming formal release.

A new formal release that violates the approved repository convention
without an active approved exception is noncompliant with EMS-CTRL-038.

Historical legacy tags alone do not cause current EMS-CTRL-038
noncompliance.

rows.normative_requirement: Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) apply only where the service approved business continuity, disaster recovery, customer, regulatory, or service-classification requirements establish such objectives.
